name: rowMins
title: Gets the minimum of each row of a matrix

origin.description: Gets the minimum of each row of a matrix.
origin.usage:
rowMins(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, dim. = dim(x), ...,
  useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The installed function returns a vector of length N, one minimum per selected row, in the order of cols. When x is integer and every selected row has a non-missing value, the result stays integer. A row with no counted value makes the whole result double, and that row is +Inf. For doubles, R's NA stops that row. A plain NaN is stored and later finite values do not replace it.
origin.value: A vector of length N. The mode is integer when x is integer and every row counted a value, and double otherwise.

translation.description: Gets the minimum of each row of a matrix.
translation.usage: rowMins(x, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False, dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix. Integer values stay on the integer path. Floating values are computed as float64. Logical input is rejected.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. The scan walks the selected columns in this order.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm. False keeps R's NA and a plain NaN.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x. A 1-d x is filled in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain array, with no names attached.

translation.details: The scan lives in the Rust crate rowranges, ported from matrixStats src/rowRanges.c with what 0 and hasNA TRUE. R's NA is a NaN whose low 32 bits are 1954: that payload is copied and the rest of the row is skipped when na_rm is false. A plain NaN is stored, later finite values do not replace it, and a later NaN overwrites the minimum with its own payload. A row with no counted value is +Inf. Integer input returns int32 when every row counted a value. If any row counted nothing, the whole result is float64.
translation.value: A vector of length N. Floating input returns float64. Integer input returns int32 when every selected row has a non-missing value, and float64 otherwise.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowranges import rowMins

x = np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F")
rowMins(x)
